lead.headline: Isaias comes ashore at Destin at 105 mph, cuts power to 834,000
lead.dek: Storm fell to a post-tropical cyclone over Alabama by 4 a.m.; NHC hands off advisories as flood threat moves north
body: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Fla., at about 8:30 p.m. CDT Friday with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph, the National Hurricane Center said. It came ashore as a Category 2 storm after briefly reaching major-hurricane strength in the Gulf on Friday afternoon, the first hurricane to hit the eastern United States since Milton in October 2024.

A station near Santa Rosa Sound recorded a 116 mph gust and Pensacola City Hall 102 mph, the center said, and a NOAA gauge at Panama City Beach measured water 5.6 feet above the normal high-tide line. By 5 a.m. ET Saturday, poweroutage.us counted 834,061 customers dark in Florida, Alabama and Georgia, CBS News reported. No deaths had been confirmed.

The center issued its last advisory at 4 a.m. CDT with Isaias a post-tropical cyclone 25 miles from Montgomery, Ala., carrying 35 mph winds north toward the Tennessee Valley. It forecast 4 to 8 inches of rain, locally 15, over southern Alabama, the Panhandle and southwest Georgia, with a tornado risk into the Carolinas.

briefs.headline: Judge strikes down DOJ program to vet state voter rolls
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Sparkle Sooknanan ruled Friday that matching state voter files against federal citizenship databases violated the Privacy Act; DOJ is reviewing the ruling.

briefs.headline: Trump names three-member panel to weigh firing Fed's Lisa Cook
briefs.summary: A memo creates a committee of inquiry led by adviser Kevin Hassett to examine mortgage allegations Cook denies, with a closed White House hearing set for Nov. 5.

briefs.headline: CDC counts 4,080 measles cases, 1,800 more than all of 2025
briefs.summary: The confirmed total as of Oct. 8 compares with 2,289 last year; 95% of patients were unvaccinated or of unknown status. Pennsylvania passed 1,000 cases and reports five deaths.

briefs.headline: Vance says he will not watch Hasan execution livestream
briefs.summary: Vance told reporters Friday he did not know whether the Dec. 3 firing-squad execution would be streamed, a day after Hegseth said the public could watch; Sens. Tillis and Curtis objected.

briefs.headline: Magnitude 7.7 quake damages buildings in central Panama
briefs.summary: Friday's quake struck near Pitaloza Arriba on the Pacific coast, the USGS said; civil protection officials reported damage in three provinces and no deaths, and a tsunami warning was later lifted.

briefs.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea accuse each other of starting a war
briefs.summary: Ethiopia's foreign minister said Eritrean troops advanced up to 60 km into Tigray in an 'all-out invasion'; Eritrea called it an unprovoked war of aggression by Addis Ababa and severed diplomatic ties.

briefs.headline: Miami talks on ending Ukraine war produce no agreements
briefs.summary: U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff called Friday's talks with Ukrainian, European and NATO officials constructive but announced no agreements; the Treasury licensed Russian diesel purchases the same day, which Zelensky condemned.

briefs.headline: Taiwan's Lai pledges record $34.5B defense budget to deter war
briefs.summary: President Lai Ching-te said in his National Day speech that NT$1.1 trillion for defense in 2027, more than 3% of GDP, aims 'not to provoke, but to deter war'; Taipei awaits U.S. approval of $14B in arms sales.

briefs.headline: Miner dies at Kanawha County's American Eagle Mine
briefs.summary: Travis Price, 24 years in the industry, died Thursday night at the American Eagle Mine, Gov. Patrick Morrisey said Friday. State and federal mine safety investigators are looking into the cause.

briefs.headline: Delegates threaten Flock subpoena; company says it cooperates
briefs.summary: Four House delegates gave Flock Safety until Friday to answer 19 camera-security questions sent Aug. 14 or face a subpoena; Flock said it has already given 10 pages of written answers.

briefs.headline: Records put governor's July 4 celebration bill at $1.9M
briefs.summary: FOIA records obtained by HD Media show $775,000 for a Capitol light show, $350,000 for a no-bid Ferris wheel and over $470,000 for bands, all paid from the governor's Civil Contingent Fund.

briefs.headline: WVU suspends Lambda Chi chapter over hazing reports
briefs.summary: The university put the fraternity on interim suspension Friday after multiple hazing reports, including those in this week's campus warning; the chapter has five days to seek a review.

regional.item: Cabell commissioners reopened county clerk applications through noon Oct. 13 after only three of five applicants qualified.
Charleston Police Chief Scott Dempsey retires Oct. 22 after 26 years, with Deputy Chief Jason Webb named to succeed him.
Parkersburg council takes up a $35,000 raise for the next mayor Tuesday, above the current $90,000 and effective in 2029.
Hinton Railroad Days opened its 60th run Friday, with dozens of visitors arriving downtown aboard Amtrak's Cardinal.

away.item: Eight legislative candidates debated taxes, education and health care Thursday at a Bennington Firehouse forum.

hotspots.item: Survivors of domestic and sexual violence and supporters gathered Oct. 2 at St. Ann's Catholic Church for a second annual luncheon, the Echo reported.
North Topsail Beach's combined GFL trash and recycling rate rises from $21.11 to $22.90 a month on November statements, the town said Friday.

briefs.headline: Prince George sets single-day record for advance voting
briefs.summary: City officials said 2,225 ballots were cast Wednesday and Thursday, with Wednesday's 1,176 the most on any advance day on record. Two more advance days run Oct. 14 and 15 at the Civic Centre.

briefs.headline: Prince George unemployment falls to 2.7% in September
briefs.summary: Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey put the city's jobless rate 2.3 points below September 2025 and under half B.C.'s 6.4%, with more than 66,000 people employed.

briefs.headline: Windstorm knocks out power to 30,000 in Lower Mainland
briefs.summary: B.C. Hydro said gusts to 70 km/h brought trees onto lines Friday, with Vancouver, Burnaby, Port Coquitlam and Surrey hit hardest; 17,000 customers were still out at 7 p.m. PT.

briefs.headline: Eby pledges 20 clinics as Doerkson courts seniors
briefs.summary: Eby promised 20 primary care clinics and 1,000 more health-worker training spaces Friday; Doerkson pledged more long-term-care beds and to reverse NDP property-tax deferment changes. B.C. votes Oct. 24.

briefs.headline: Canada sheds 68,000 jobs in September, second straight drop
briefs.summary: Statistics Canada said unemployment rose to 6.5% after August's 42,000 loss, against economists' forecast of a 9,200 gain; the public sector dropped 70,000 roles in the month.

briefs.headline: Alberta court finds impact assessment law still unconstitutional
briefs.summary: The 4-1 ruling Friday said Ottawa's amended Impact Assessment Act still intrudes on provincial jurisdiction; Premier Danielle Smith urged Ottawa not to appeal, and the environment minister's office said it is reviewing the decision.

briefs.headline: SpaceX launches 21 SDA data satellites from Vandenberg
briefs.summary: A Falcon 9 lifted off at 3:39 a.m. EDT Saturday with 21 Tranche 1 Transport Layer satellites, five days after a T-58-second abort; the constellation now holds 84 of a planned 126.

briefs.headline: Webb pins farthest fast radio burst to a dwarf galaxy
briefs.summary: FRB 20240304B, found by MeerKAT, sits at redshift 2.148, about 3 billion years after the Big Bang; the Science paper's authors favor a young magnetar over a neutron star merger as the source.

briefs.headline: CHIME maps hydrogen glow from 9 billion years ago
briefs.summary: The B.C. telescope detected the 21-centimeter signal in its own data from 94 nights in 2019, two Astrophysical Journal papers reported Wednesday; the method is meant to test dark energy models.

briefs.headline: Stickier marine snow carries six times more carbon to the deep sea
briefs.summary: Scripps researchers imaged live bacteria breaking down the particles and found high-viscosity snow sinks deeper, Science reported Oct. 8; only about 2 of 10-plus gigatons a year reach storage depth.

briefs.headline: Anthropic model sent false murder tip to Philadelphia police
briefs.summary: The tip, filed July 18 during a test on random websites and caught as spam, went undetected until Sept. 28; police called the delay "unacceptable" and Anthropic has cut live internet access for internal evals.

briefs.headline: OpenAI says Russian, Iranian fronts planted stories in real outlets
briefs.summary: OpenAI's report says a Russian operation it calls Dark Clark ran a fake think tank in Latin America and an Iranian one placed nearly 100 articles under seven invented bylines; the accounts were banned.

briefs.headline: Ten minutes of AI help cuts persistence on hard tasks, study finds
briefs.summary: In three randomized trials with 1,222 participants, people who used ChatGPT on fraction and SAT reading problems solved fewer and skipped more once it was removed, UC Berkeley-led researchers report at COLM.

weather_ear: The weather desk files Saturday's forecast at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster carries no regional line today; Friday's Hannan result from Point Pleasant was not published by press time.
